cards.back: To succeed in reaching a particular goal or standard through effort. Example: 'Students who study consistently achieve higher scores on standardized tests.'
To gain or obtain something, especially knowledge or a skill. Example: 'She acquired fluency in English after living abroad for two years.'
To change or adjust in order to suit different conditions. Example: 'International students must adapt to new academic environments when they study overseas.'
Enough in quantity or good enough in quality for a particular purpose. Example: 'The library provides adequate resources for undergraduate research.'
To have an influence on or cause a change in something. Example: 'Climate change affects agricultural productivity in many developing countries.'
One of two or more available possibilities or choices. Example: 'Public transport is a practical alternative to driving in congested cities.'
To examine something in detail in order to understand it or explain it. Example: 'Researchers analyze survey data to identify patterns in consumer behavior.'
A way of dealing with a situation or problem. Example: 'The government adopted a new approach to reducing urban pollution.'
Suitable or proper in the circumstances. Example: 'It is appropriate to use formal language when writing an academic essay.'
A subject, field of study, or range of activity. Example: 'Environmental science is a growing area of research at many universities.'
A particular part or feature of something. Example: 'One important aspect of language learning is regular practice with native speakers.'
To help or support someone in doing something. Example: 'Teaching assistants help assist students who are struggling with coursework.'
To accept something as true without proof or confirmation. Example: 'We should not assume that all students have access to the internet at home.'
The power or right to give orders, make decisions, or enforce rules. Example: 'Local authorities are responsible for maintaining public schools in most countries.'
Able to be used or obtained; at someone's disposal. Example: 'Scholarships are available for students who demonstrate strong academic performance.'
Having knowledge or understanding of a situation or fact. Example: 'Many people are not aware of the health risks associated with a sedentary lifestyle.'
An advantage or profit gained from something. Example: 'One major benefit of exercise is that it improves both physical and mental health.'
A class or group of things having shared characteristics. Example: 'The survey divided respondents into three age categories for analysis.'
A main division of a book or a distinct period in history or in a person's life. Example: 'The final chapter of the textbook covers advanced statistical methods.'
A condition or fact that affects a situation. Example: 'Economic circumstances often determine whether young people can attend university.'
An official group of people given authority to investigate or control something. Example: 'The education commission recommended significant reforms to the national curriculum.'
A group of people living in the same area or sharing common interests. Example: 'The local community raised funds to build a new public library.'
Consisting of many interconnected parts; not simple or straightforward. Example: 'Climate change is a complex issue that requires cooperation between many nations.'
An abstract idea or general notion. Example: 'The concept of sustainability has become central to modern urban planning.'
To bring something to an end, or to reach a judgment after consideration. Example: 'The researchers concluded that regular reading improves vocabulary acquisition.'
To organize and carry out an activity or process. Example: 'The university plans to conduct a survey on student satisfaction this semester.'
Following as a result or effect of something. Example: 'The factory closure and the consequent job losses affected the entire region.'
To be composed or made up of specified elements. Example: 'The exam consists of four sections: reading, writing, listening, and speaking.'
To form or make up a whole or a specified part of it. Example: 'International students constitute nearly thirty percent of the student body.'
The circumstances or setting in which an event occurs or a statement is made. Example: 'Words can have different meanings depending on the context in which they are used.'
A written or spoken agreement that is intended to be enforceable by law. Example: 'Employees should read their contract carefully before signing it.'
To give something, especially money or ideas, in order to help achieve something. Example: 'Volunteers contribute their time and skills to support community programs.'
To bring something into existence that did not exist before. Example: 'The government aims to create more job opportunities for young graduates.'
Facts and statistics collected together for reference or analysis. Example: 'The data shows a significant increase in online shopping over the past decade.'
To state or describe the exact nature or scope of something. Example: 'It is important to clearly define key terms at the beginning of an essay.'
To clearly show the existence or truth of something by giving proof or evidence. Example: 'The experiment demonstrated that plants grow faster under artificial light.'
To obtain something from a specified source. Example: 'Many English words are derived from Latin and Greek roots.'
To give shares of something or spread it over an area. Example: 'The organization distributes free textbooks to schools in rural areas.'
The system of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a country or region. Example: 'Tourism plays a vital role in the economy of many island nations.'
The natural world, or the surrounding conditions in which a person lives or operates. Example: 'Protecting the environment is one of the most pressing challenges of our time.'
To set up or create something on a firm or permanent basis. Example: 'The university was established in 1850 and has grown significantly since then.'
To roughly calculate or judge the value, number, or extent of something. Example: 'Experts estimate that the world population will reach ten billion by 2050.'
To assess or judge the value or quality of something. Example: 'Teachers evaluate student progress through regular assignments and examinations.'
The available facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true. Example: 'There is strong evidence that regular exercise reduces the risk of heart disease.'
To send goods or services to another country for sale. Example: 'Brazil exports large quantities of coffee to markets around the world.'
A circumstance, fact, or influence that contributes to a result. Example: 'Cost is an important factor when choosing a university to attend.'
A distinctive attribute or aspect of something. Example: 'An important feature of academic writing is the use of formal language.'
The management of large amounts of money, especially by governments or large companies. Example: 'She decided to study finance because she was interested in how banks operate.'
A fixed or conventional method for doing or producing something. Example: 'There is no simple formula for success in learning a foreign language.'
The purpose or role that something is designed to serve. Example: 'The main function of the introduction is to present the topic and thesis statement.'
A sum of money given by a government or organization for a particular purpose. Example: 'The research team received a grant to study the effects of air pollution on health.'
To recognize or establish what something is. Example: 'The study aimed to identify the main causes of stress among university students.'
To explain or make something clear by using examples or comparisons. Example: 'The professor used several case studies to illustrate the concept of supply and demand.'
A marked effect or influence on something. Example: 'Social media has had a significant impact on the way people communicate.'
To suggest something indirectly rather than stating it openly. Example: 'The results imply that diet has a stronger influence on health than previously thought.'
To point out or show something. Example: 'Recent surveys indicate that more young people are choosing to study abroad.'
A single person, considered separately from a group. Example: 'Each individual is responsible for managing their own time during the examination.'
To cause physical harm or damage to someone. Example: 'Several workers were injured in the factory accident last month.'
An organization established for a particular purpose, especially research or education. Example: 'The institute conducts research on renewable energy technologies.'
To explain the meaning of information or actions. Example: 'Students must learn how to interpret graphs and charts in academic texts.'
To put money or effort into something with the expectation of a return or benefit. Example: 'Many countries invest heavily in education to develop their workforce.'
To include something as a necessary part or result. Example: 'Learning a language involves regular practice, patience, and dedication.'
An important topic or problem for discussion or debate. Example: 'Environmental pollution is a critical issue that governments must address.'
An individual thing or unit, especially one that is part of a list or collection. Example: 'Each item on the reading list is essential for the final examination.'
A newspaper, magazine, or academic publication dealing with a particular subject. Example: 'The findings were published in a leading medical journal last year.'
To show or prove that something is right, reasonable, or necessary. Example: 'You must justify your answer with evidence from the reading passage.'
Work, especially physical work, or the workers in a country or industry. Example: 'The construction industry depends on a large supply of skilled labor.'
A sheet or thickness of material covering a surface or forming one of several levels. Example: 'The atmosphere is made up of several distinct layers, each with different characteristics.'
Relating to or permitted by the law. Example: 'All citizens have the legal right to access free primary education.'
To make or enact laws. Example: 'The government plans to legislate against discrimination in the workplace.'
In the same way; also or similarly. Example: 'Reading improves writing skills; likewise, writing regularly can enhance reading comprehension.'
A connection or relationship between two or more things. Example: 'Research has shown a clear link between poverty and poor educational outcomes.'
To discover the exact position of something, or to situate something in a particular place. Example: 'The new campus is located near the city center for easy access by public transport.'
Reasoning conducted according to strict principles of validity. Example: 'A strong essay should follow a clear line of logic from introduction to conclusion.'
Relating to a group of people who share a common cultural background or nationality. Example: 'The city is known for its ethnic diversity, with residents from over fifty different countries.'
To promise with certainty that something will happen or is true. Example: 'A university degree does not guarantee employment, but it improves career prospects.'
